# ethereum-optimism/specs Daily Update (Mar 26, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
The day saw significant progress in addressing flaky tests and refining L2 contract upgrade mechanisms. Several issues related to L2CM upgrades were closed, indicating advancements in the upgrade system's robustness and tooling. Discussions on active issues focused on test flakiness, interop transaction eviction, and structural improvements to the upgrade pipeline.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

No new features, bug fixes, code refactoring, documentation enhancements, or tests were added today.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### L2 Contract Upgrade Tooling and Feature Flag Implementation
Several issues related to the L2 Contract Manager (L2CM) upgrades were closed. This includes the creation of a Solidity script for deterministic JSON NUT bundle generation ([#18834](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18834)), the implementation of development feature flag support in the L2 upgrade system ([#18838](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18838)), and the addition of `just` commands for generating NUT bundles ([#18840](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18840)) and running L2 upgrade fork tests ([#18841](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18841)). These closures indicate a maturing of the L2CM upgrade process and associated developer tooling.

### Flaky Test Resolution
A flaky test, `TestCLELDivergence`, was closed ([#19681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19681)). The discussion leading to its closure suggested that a fix had been implemented in a related pull request, and the issue could be reopened if the flake reappeared. Another flaky test, `TestPreinteropFaultProofs_TraceExtensionActivation`, was also closed ([#19760](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19760)), with a related PR expected to resolve the underlying nonce race condition.

## NEW ISSUES

### Breaking Change in `StorageKeys` Value
A new issue was opened regarding a breaking change in the `StorageKeys` value in `op-geth` v1.101701.0, where `null` is returned instead of `[]` ([#780](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/780)). This is attributed to `SortedFunc` in Go causing empty arrays to be returned as `nil`.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Flaky Test: `TestCLELDivergence` ([#19681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19681))
This issue, though closed today, had extensive discussion. Initially, the flakiness was investigated, with ajsutton suggesting it might be a real bug related to the derivation pipeline resetting the `StatusTracker`'s `UnsafeL2` back to an earlier state. pcw109550 provided a detailed analysis, concluding that the observed reset was likely part of the initial derivation pipeline lifecycle and not an issue during EL sync. They suggested the test's comment was incorrect and that the reset was expected behavior. The issue was ultimately closed, with ajsutton suggesting it could be reopened if the flake recurs.

### Flaky Test: `TestPreinteropFaultProofs_TraceExtensionActivation` ([#19760](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19760))
This newly opened flaky test issue quickly saw discussion. ajsutton identified that a related pull request ([#19745](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19745)) is expected to fix this flake. The root cause was explained as a nonce race condition between two transaction-sending mechanisms during the `migrateSuperRoots` process, where `PendingNonceAt` could return a stale value, leading to transaction replacement and migration failure. The PR's solution, using EIP-7702 SetCode transactions, eliminates this race by simplifying the migration and avoiding ownership reassignments.

### Contracts: Prove Withdrawals Using Chain-Specific Root Claim ([#18517](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18517))
ajsutton inquired whether this issue could be closed, as the approach might have changed to use `rootClaimByChainId` based on the game type. This suggests a potential resolution or re-evaluation of the original requirement.

### [L2CM] Investigate Adding an Array of Predeploys to Increase Upgrade Safety ([#19260](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19260))
maurelian provided a detailed analysis of a structural pipeline gap in the L2CM upgrade process. While an immediate bug (omission of `L2DevFeatureFlags` from the NUT bundle) was fixed by PR #19464, a deeper structural issue remains. The problem stems from distributed knowledge across multiple data structures for implementation deployment, leading to potential desynchronization. The current fork tests, while helpful, have limitations as they iterate proxies rather than the full `Implementations` struct and validate outcomes rather than pipeline completeness. A latent issue with `ConditionalDeployer` was also highlighted, where a future bytecode change could brick batch upgrades due to a similar structural gap.

### Document Interop Tx Pool Eviction Behavior on Reorg ([#19351](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19351))
pcw109550 raised a question regarding the eviction of interop transactions from the mempool during reorgs. Specifically, they asked whether the mempool explicitly iterates and drops interop transactions or if periodic re-evaluation handles this, given that `op-geth#772` drops executing messages that were supposed to be reinjected.

### Remove Karst-Specific Upgrade Transactions from GenerateNUTBundle ([#19369](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19369))
0xOneTony provided an important note for when the Karst-specific transactions are removed. They highlighted that `UpgradeUtils.getTransactionCount()` must also be updated to reflect the removal of three Karst-only transactions (ConditionalDeployer deployment, ConditionalDeployer upgrade, ProxyAdmin upgrade), and related fields in the `GasLimits` struct and `gasLimits()` function should also be removed.
